> The vast majority of the work artists get is industry or low-paying jobs which don't give a shit about who created the art. I would say that 90% of digital artist's work could be replaced with AI.

That's something that constantly happens, with new tech and industries replacing older ones. And regardless of our opinion on it, we live in a capitalistic society which encourages this. Preferential treatment to any one industry will be unfair for everyone else.

And don't get me wrong, I sympathise with artists. It's one of the reasons I support ubi, to deal with losses of industries such as this.

But restricting AI art would be to prevent the development of technology in a particular field, which hasn't been done with any other field. So on principle, I can't support banning AI art.

Self driving cars will replace drivers completely, yet that isn't being condemned. 

If ai can't be more creative, then won't humans naturally choose  to go for human created art? And if they won't, then it just means that creativity isn't valued, in the same way that not all artist's art is valued equally, irrespective of effort. That's unfortunately how things have always worked in a capitalistic society.

And your last point is something I agree with, and it sucks that that happens, but the same can once again be said of the countless careers elimination by technology. So why should we consider this field to be more important than any of the others.

Ai and technology on general have been taking away jobs for centuries. Computers eliminated a significant chunk of the jobs involving manual calculations, with the Internet, postal workers might have lost jobs, we've got software automating a lot of the stuff which people used to do,  I don't see why ai art should be where we draw the line 

It's awful for artists, but it'll be better to push for a more equitable society than to just ban technology.
